answer: A verifier validates a fresh, hardware-rooted attestation showing that an agent runs approved enclave code with the expected MRENCLAVE, then binds its key to the attested instance. MRENCLAVE identifies code, not a unique device, so Sybil resistance also requires non-exportable, hardware-bound keys and controlled enrollment. This impedes VM duplication, while scaling identities may require more physical silicon; summit, mirror, and atlas policies should preserve that distinction.
